We need to implement reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover. Standard reduction: Given graph G with n vertices, edges E, and parameter k for Clique, construct graph G' same vertices, same edges, and set k' = n - k for Vertex Cover. Since a set of vertices is a vertex cover of size ≤ n - k iff its complement is a clique of size ≥ k. So reduction is trivial: same graph, convert k.

Edge cases need to match definitions. For Clique: yes if k <=0 always yes; k=1 yes if n>=1; k>n always no. For VertexCover: yes if k>=n always yes; k<0 always no; empty graph yes for any k>=0.

Our reduction: given instance I = {"n": n, "edges": ..., "k": k}. Return {"n": n, "edges": same, "k": n - k}. Need to ensure that the answer equivalence holds for all edge cases. Let's test:

- If k <=0: Clique always yes. Then n - k >= n, possibly > n, but vertex cover instance with k' >= n => yes (since k' >= n). Good.

- If k = 1 and n>=1: Clique yes. Then k' = n-1. Since n-1 < n, but vertex cover instance: does a vertex cover of size ≤ n-1 always exist? For any graph, you can cover all edges by taking all vertices except maybe one isolated vertex? Actually worst case a complete graph requires n-1 vertices to cover all edges? Complete graph: need n-1 vertices, so yes. But for any graph, vertex cover size ≤ n-1 always holds because you can take all vertices except any one; that covers all edges because any edge has two endpoints, at least one is not the excluded vertex unless edge is between excluded vertex and another excluded? Wait we exclude only one vertex, so any edge that is incident only on the excluded vertex would not be covered, but edge between excluded vertex and some other vertex is covered by the other vertex. Edge between two excluded vertices impossible because only one excluded. So all edges are covered. So vertex cover size ≤ n-1 always yes. So k' = n-1 => yes. Good.

- If k > n: Clique no. Then k' = n - k < 0. Vertex cover instance with k' < 0 always no. Good.

Thus reduction works.

Implement brute-force: For Clique, check all subsets of vertices size >= k, test if all pairs edges exist. For VertexCover, check subsets size <= k that cover all edges.

class Clique:

        [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
      * k is any integer.

    Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
    edge between every two of them.

    Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
    always no.

    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        validate_graph_with_k(instance)


class VertexCover:
    """Vertex Cover.

    Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
      * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
        [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
      * k is any integer.

    Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
    k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
    every edge.
